## kb_to_source

- Sentence-by-sentence sweep: every normative claim of the 52 documents has a structured source (base rule, eligibility, variant parameter/schema description, measure, event grain, extended rule/overwrite/ladder, tool docstring). Rationale clauses used by task 1's factors are source text.
- Additions: none. Omissions: none. Rewrites changing meaning: none.
- Cross-problem operational guidance in the income-loss hub or any other document: none (no tool of another problem named; no "first pay …").
- Task opening world state written as policy fact: none. The hypothetical figures in task-1-relevant docs (e.g. 1400.00, 2000.00, 1600.00, 2100.00) are not task 1's values (task values 1890, 2600, 1450, 9 nights, etc. do not occur).

Policy-side notes (not KB verdicts):
1. `variants[*].income_loss_basis` ("nightly_subtotal of each confirmed stay the host had to cancel …") is rendered faithfully in category_sublimits_and_lost_income_cover ("How lost income is valued (every level)"), while the extended rule starts from the claims team's verified loss and the base passage using the nightly subtotal with the max-nights cap is retired. In task 1 the verified loss equals the cancelled booking's nightly subtotal (1890.00) and 7/9 × 1890.00 equals 7 × 210.00, so no alternative changes the figure; the residual parameter is a policy-side tidiness issue (same family as the depreciation_schedule / guest_payment_offset note in `0.md`).
2. "Settlement date" undefined in words in source and KB; no task-1 tier depends on it (no Superhost or 12-month condition binds for a Professional Host on an Entire Home).
